in_arabic.name: شَقُور
in_arabic.meaning: رقيق العفو و اللطف و الرحمة
in_arabic.long_meaning: ينحدر هذا الاسم من الجذر (ش ق ر) الذي يرمز إلى روح الفضل و الرحمة. يصف الاسم شخصاً رقيق العفو و اللطف و الرحمة، و هو من أهم الجوانب الدينية في الإسلام. يعتبر شاقور عنواناً للفضائل و النزاهة و الرحمة في الإسلام، و هو ما يجعل منه اسمًا مميزاً و مرنًا في التقاليد الإسلامية.

in_urdu.name: شَقُور
in_urdu.long_meaning: یہ نام جذر (ش ق ر) سے ماخوذ ہے جس میں فضل اور رحمت کی روح ہے۔ نام کے معنی ہیں دلتذ و فضل اور رحمت  جس کی وجہ سے ہے یہ نام مسلمانوں میں بہت مقبول ہے۔

in_hindi.name: शक़ूर
in_hindi.long_meaning: यह नाम जड़ (शक़) से मिलता है जिसका अर्थ है दयालु व मृदु व्यक्ति। इस नाम के माध्यम से व्यक्ति की दयालुता व मृदुता की विशेषता को दर्शाया जाता है।

in_pashto.name: شَقُور
in_pashto.long_meaning: دا نام د (ش ق ر) جګر له ماخذ دی چی دا د رحمتو او ډول لپاره یوه اړخ لري. دا ډول د اسلامي دینو یوه اړخ دی چي دا د اسلامي دینو څخه تر ټولو لوی وده ده.

data.cultural_impact: The name Shaqoor carries an aura of power and strength, making it an auspicious name in Arab and Islamic cultures. It is believed that those named Shaqoor are blessed with enhanced physical and mental abilities that allow them to tackle life's challenges with confidence and determination. In a collective sense, Shaqoor symbolizes valor and resilience, components that contribute to the racial and ethnic identities of many Muslim communities.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Shaqoor represents the inner strength that comes from a deep connection with Allah (God). For Muslims, spiritual strength is an essential aspect of personal growth and development, allowing individuals to endure trials and strive towards achieving their goals in accordance with Islamic teachings. Shaqoor is a reminder that every individual possesses immense inner potential and power, inviting believers to tap into this inner strength and seek Allah's guidance in moments of uncertainty or difficulty.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah The name Shaqoor carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.time_period: Year 45 of Prophet Muhammad's Prophethood (626 AD)
historical_references.context: The name Shaqoor was given to a man from the Banu Hanifah tribe who was a supporter of the Muslim cause. He was known for his extreme bravery and dedication to Islam. During the Battle of the Trench (Khandaq), he led a group of Muslims to reinforce the front line, where they faced the Jewish tribes of Banu Nadir and Banu Qurayzah. Shaqoor's bravery helped the Muslims secure their position, and he ultimately sacrificed his life in this battle.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Baladhuri's Ansab Al-Ashraf The name Shaqoor carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.time_period: Year 56 of Prophet Muhammad's Prophethood (631 AD)
historical_references.context: Shaqoor was also the name of a companion of Prophet Muhammad who was known for his generosity and piety. He was a wealthy man who would often distribute his wealth among the needy. During the Battle of Hunayn, Prophet Muhammad appointed Shaqoor as the commander of the right flank of the Muslim army. Shaqoor's leadership and bravery helped the Muslims secure a decisive victory over the Hawazin and Thamud tribes.
